source: operator-confirmed table, superseding the handwritten note in capture_20260830_234933_photo
revision_history: v1 2026-08-30: 5.5 x 3.75 x 3.5 m estimate. Superseded — 24 cm out on ceiling, ~45 cm out on wall length, and rectangular-only.
v2 2026-08-30: per-wall, heights 325.4/325.9 varying by 0.5 cm, window height 110.5. Superseded.
v3 2026-08-31: heights corrected to a uniform 329.4 (+3.75 cm on v2), window height 110.9. Wall lengths and floor unchanged.

v4 2026-08-31: second door added on wall C (1.850 x 0.855 m, identical to the wall D door). The 40 cm floor-versus-wall gap is resolved: it is two 20 cm door reveals, i.e. the wall thickness visible inside each door opening. 497.7 - 2x20 = 457.7 exactly.
v5 2026-08-31: third door added on wall B, 1.850 m high x 2.013 m wide. Four openings total.
v6 2026-08-31: the wall B and wall C openings are archways, not doors. Wall D keeps the only real door. Two archways means two adjacencies out of this room.

v7 2026-08-31: openings relaid. Walls A, B, D carry openings; wall C carries only the window. Wall A has the largest opening (1.850 x 2.013 m). A and B are archways, D is the hinged door. This layout also resolves the 40 cm exactly.
v8 2026-08-31: wall B archway measured at 1.850 x 0.855 m, confirming the inferred width. Both archways lead to the Hall, from different directions, so Living room and Hall are connected twice.

v9 2026-08-31: operator confirmed archway A is 1.850 m high x 2.013 m wide (wider than tall, as recorded) and the 0.20 m wall thickness. Every Living room figure is now measured or operator-confirmed; none is inferred.

v10 2026-08-31: annotated sketch (capture_20260831_021355_photo) shows archway_b leads to the bathroom below the Living room, not to the Hall. Supersedes the earlier statement that both archways lead to the Hall.
v11 2026-08-31: tape uncertainty measured by repeat readings. Ground truth now carries per-quantity uncertainty instead of implying exactness.
units_note: Source values are centimetres, recorded here in metres.
ceiling_note: All four corners now measure identically, so the ground truth asserts a flat ceiling and the full 1.5 cm gate is available to the pipeline. This replaces v2, which showed a 0.5 cm corner-to-corner spread; that spread was an artefact of the superseded numbers, not a property of the room.
shape_note: Walls A and C differ by 8.0 cm (1.6%) while B and D agree exactly. The room is genuinely not square, which is why per-wall ground truth is required.

openings.note: Wall C's only opening. A window does not reach the floor, so it takes no reveal off any floor run.

Largest opening in the room, 2.013 m of wall A's 5.057 m run, and the only opening here wider than it is tall - confirmed by the operator rather than assumed, since the proportion is unusual enough to have been a transposed height and width. Open archway leading to the Hall.

Leads to the bathroom below the Living room, per the annotated sketch. An earlier description had both archways going to the Hall; the sketch's door arrows and the Hall's own opening list both contradict that, and the Hall has no 0.855 m opening anywhere.
The only hinged door. Closed-leaf openings carry no through-view, so this one gives the photo tier no adjacency evidence.

open_questions: Tape uncertainty: re-measure one wall and one opening three times and take the spread. Until then we cannot quote a ground-truth interval, and any pipeline error smaller than that spread is unmeasurable.
Ground truth for the Hall, so the double-archway loop can be scored rather than only described.
method_note: Tape. Uncertainty is not yet quantified: a single-pass tape run over a ~5 m wall carries sag, corner placement and reading error, and the opening gate is 2 cm. Cheapest way to pin it is to re-measure one wall and one opening three times and take the spread — until then we cannot honestly quote a ground-truth interval, and any pipeline error smaller than that spread is unmeasurable.
openings_note: Four openings: window on C, archways on A and B, hinged door on D. Two archways is two adjacencies out of this room. With four openings the >=85% opening-width gate rounds up to 100% - three of four is 75% and fails - so every opening must land within 2 cm and a phantom fifth fails the row on its own.
wall_thickness_note: Confirmed at 0.20 m. It was originally derived from the 40 cm floor-versus-wall gap divided by two reveals, so confirming it independently closes that reasoning rather than leaving a measured quantity resting on an inference. Consistent with masonry construction and the 3.294 m ceiling.

floor_vs_wall.explanation: The long floor run is measured wall B face to wall D face. B carries an archway and D carries a door, so there is an opening at each end of that run, each with a 0.20 m reveal. 457.7 + 20 + 20 = 497.7, which is wall C exactly.
floor_vs_wall.wall_a_note: Wall A measures 5.057 m, 8 cm longer than the reconciled 4.977 m. That is the room not being square, already recorded, not a second unexplained gap.
floor_vs_wall.short_run_note: The short floor run is 3.330 m and equals walls B and D exactly. Wall C's only opening is a window, which does not reach the floor, so nothing shortens this run.
floor_vs_wall.scoring_consequence: A reconstruction sees the room-side wall surface and should recover 4.977 m for wall C and 5.057 m for wall A. Scoring either against the 4.577 m clear floor would report an 8% error that is really two doorways. Floor area must be computed from wall lengths.

adjacency.note: All four openings now have a destination. Three lead somewhere, one is a window.
adjacency.loop_note: The property's cycle survives, in a better form. It is no longer two parallel archways between the same pair, but a triangle: Hall to Living room, Living room to bathroom_2, bathroom_2 back to the Hall. A three-room cycle is the stronger test - it constrains an intermediate room's placement too, so the residual reflects error accumulated over two hops rather than one.

completeness.ceiling: measured, flat across all four corners
completeness.openings: 4 of 4 measured, each assigned to a wall, types confirmed
completeness.adjacency: 2 edges recorded, both to the Hall
completeness.remaining: tape uncertainty is still unquantified; the Hall end of the loop is unmeasured

tape_uncertainty.protocol: Same quantity measured three times, tape fully retracted and re-placed between readings.

verdict_against_gates.wall_length: usable - sd 1.56 cm against a 40 cm gate (+/-8% of a 5 m wall), 4% of it
verdict_against_gates.opening_width: MARGINAL - sd 0.99 cm against a 2 cm gate, half of it
verdict_against_gates.opening_height: unmeasurable - sd 2.89 cm exceeds the 2 cm gate
verdict_against_gates.ceiling_height: UNMEASURABLE - sd 14.01 cm is 9.3x the 1.5 cm gate

recorded_values_outside_their_repeat_ran: Wall A recorded 505.7, repeat range 507.0-510.1. The recorded value sits below every repeat reading.
Door width recorded 85.5, repeat range 88.2-90.0. The recorded value sits 2.7 cm below every repeat reading.
tape_uncertainty.interpretation: Two of four recorded quantities fall outside the range of their own repeats, so the original single readings carry a bias on top of the random spread, not just noise. Recorded values are kept as the answer key because they were taken systematically across all walls in one session, but they are now quoted with uncertainty rather than as exact figures.
